                              scores: Antigua, Australia, Bahamas, Belize, British Islands, Cameroon (University

                        complete the housing application.

will need to be filled out by the exchange students and sent to the Institute for
                        International Studies. If you would like to send a faxed copy, that will be fine;

DS-2019 Information Form
will need to be filled out by the exchange students and sent to the Institute for
                        International Studies. If you would like to send a faxed copy, that will be fine;
                        however, we will eventually need the official copy of this form.
Proof of Health Insurance
This can be shown upon arrival. Students may also purchase insurance from Murray State
                        University upon their arrival. If you decide to purchase health insurance from Murray
                        State University, it will cost approximately $863 for one year worth of coverage.

                        requirements. This information can be found in the Exchange Visitor Program brochure
                        that will be included in the J-1 student package you will receive after submitting
                        your student documents.

                        student information packet. One thing to note is if you bring insurance from your

                        and will have to seek reimbursement once you return home.

Checklist for Exchange Students
After you have received acceptance at your university, you will need to complete and
                  submit the following materials to Murray State University:
International Student Admission Application
DS-2019 Information Form
Transcript Release Form
Language Proficiency Requirements:
IELTS overall score of 6.0 (5.5 for full admission with condition)
TOEFL overall score of 71 (61
for full admission with condition
)
SAT score of 960
GTEC overall score of 1190 (1100
for full admission with condition)
PTE overall score of 51 (45
for full admission with condition)
Duolingo English Test overall score of 100 or higher (
90
for full admission with condition)
TOEIC overall score of 790 or higher with 160 or higher speaking ( 700 with 140 or
                           higher speaking for full admission with condition)
Kaplan English Certificate Advanced Level (Higher Intermediate Level for full admission
                           with condition)
Admission to or Completion of the ESL Program at Murray State University OR
British / Cambridge International Examinations: GCE, GCSE, IGCSE, AICE, HIGCSE certificate
                           with five O-Level subject passes, or a level of B-2 or higher on the Cambridge English
                           exam.
Completion of one  semester of full-time university level classes (minimum of 12 credit
                           hours) with a 2.5 GPA or higher at an accredited US institution.
Certified Transcripts of all college coursework
Financial statement providing proof of support while at Murray State
Proof of insurance (or you can purchase insurance here after your arrival)
Murray State Housing Application and Deposit of $150 (Murray State housing application
                        and deposit must be filled out online. The application cannot be processed without
                        the deposit) OR College Courts Application and Deposit of $150 (Murray State housing
                        application and deposit must be filled out online. The application cannot be processed
                        without the deposit)
Universität Regensburg students will also need to speak with the Auslandsamt about
                        required additional materials for admission to the MBA program, including TOEFL requirements,
                        GMAT and Vordiplom scores.
Degree seeking students will need to bring their original transcripts.
Please send your completed application packet and
all the documents electronically to Bill McKibben
(
bmckibben@murraystate.edu
) or
Misty Brown Lanham (
mbrown@murraystate.edu
).
As soon as you are admitted as a visiting student, we will send you a DS-2019 and
                  other arrival information. You should take the DS-2019 with you to the closest US
                  Consular Office to apply for your visa along with the following:
passport
financial statement
acceptance letter from our office
After you have made your flight arrangements, you should send your arrival information
to Bill McKibben  (
bmckibben@murraystate.edu
)
If you plan on securing health insurance from a provider in your country, you should
                  make sure it fulfills the requirements mandated for a J-1 visitor. Check the Exchange
                  Visitor Program Welcome Brochure included in your admissions packet for these requirements.
                  You can also purchase insurance after your arrival at Murray State.

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

簽名日期:_____________________

Important Changes and Notes Regarding the SDW : Sandwich 
Program (Coursework-Based Exchange) 
     NEW / Important Changes 
1. Graduate-Level Course Enrollment Restriction (Effective Spring 2027)   
 From Spring Semester 2027, undergraduate students participating in the SDW Program will 
no longer be allowed to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Students should consider this change when preparing study plans and discussing credit 
transfer arrangements with their home institution.  
 Until the Spring 2027 course list is published, students should refer to the current 
timetable for reference. 
 
2026 Grade 1 Exchange Program Exchange Program Student (Undergraduate) | Shibaura 
Institute of Technology Timetable Search 
 
 
2. Special Provision for Students from Five-Year Integrated Degree Programs 
 Students enrolled in integrated five-year degree programs may be considered academically 
equivalent to master's students during their senior years.  
 Eligible students may continue to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Partner institutions must explain which year(s) of their program are considered master's-
level equivalent.  
 Supporting documentation must be submitted through the TAO application system by the 
nominator. 
 
3. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
 Due to stricter immigration screening procedures, all student visa applicants must provide 
proof of financial capability.  
 Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be provided in 
the application system.  
 Supporting documents must be uploaded through the TAO application system.

original_evidence.text:
4. Research Activities for SDW Participants 
Eligibility 
 Only students enrolled in the SDW Program for two semesters (one academic year) are 
eligible. 
 
Requirements 
Students wishing to conduct research activities must: 
 Apply during the same application period as the REP (Research Exchange Program). 
 Obtain prior approval from the prospective academic supervisor (laboratory faculty 
member). 
 Submit the same application documents required for the REP Program, including:  
o Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
o Research Proposal 
o Any other required supporting documents 
 Pay the facility usage fee specified in the REP Program application guidelines. 
 
Important Notes 
 Research activities will only be permitted after all required application procedures have 
been completed and approved. 
 Final approval is subject to review by both the University and the prospective academic 
supervisor. 
 
 
5. No Extension of the SDW Program During Enrollment  
 
 Effective from Fall 2026, students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to extend 
their participation in the Sandwich Program during their period of enrollment. Applicants 
must carefully decide at the time of application whether to register for one semester or 
two semesters. 
 Please note that students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to switch from the 
Sandwich Program to the REP Program, as stated in Item 4 above.

original_evidence.text:
Important Changes and Notes Regarding the REP 
(Research Exchange Program) 
Please ensure that the following important information is communicated to students prior to 
nomination and application for the REP Program. 
 
     NEW / Important Changes 
 
1. Simultaneous Participation in the SDW Program (Coursework -Based Exchange Program) Is 
Not Permitted （NEW） 
 
Due to the increasing number of SDW participants, SIT expects that available course capacity 
will need to be prioritized for students officially enrolled in the SDW Program. As a result, it has 
become difficult to accommodate requests from REP students who wish to enroll in courses in 
addition to their research activities. Although REP students staying for one semester were 
previously allowed to take courses upon request, this arrangement will no longer be available. 
Accordingly: 
• Students participating in the REP (Research Exchange Program) are not eligible to 
participate in the SDW Program (coursework -based exchange program) at the same 
time. 
• Students admitted to the REP Program will engage exclusively in research activities . 
• Course enrollment will not be permitted  for REP students. 
 
 
2. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
Beginning in July 2026, the Immigration Services Agency of Japan will implement stricter 
screening procedures for student visa applications. As a result, all students applying for a 
student visa will be required to provide documentation demonstrating sufficient financial 
resources to support themselves during their stay in Japan. 
Accordingly: 
• All student visa applicants must submit financial support documentation. 
• Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be 
provided in the application system. 
• Detailed instructions regarding the required documents will be provided through the TAO 
Online Application System. Applicants will be required to upload the designated 
supporting documents through TAO.

original_evidence.text:
5. English Language Proficiency Requirement 
The required English proficiency documentation differs depending on whether the applicant has 
already obtained preliminary acceptance from a prospective academic supervisor. 
 
■ A: Applicants Who Have Obtained Preliminary Acceptance from a Prospective Academic 
Supervisor 
 
The applicant must submit either one of the following: 
• An official English-language proficiency test score listed in the application guidelines; or 
• An email from the prospective academic supervisor confirming:  
o their preliminary acceptance of the applicant; and 
o that the applicant possesses sufficient English proficiency to conduct research 
activities. 
 
 
■ B: Applicants Without a Designated Prospective Academic Supervisor  
The applicant must submit: 
• An official English proficiency test score demonstrating CEFR B2 level or above (e.g., 
TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, or another test specified in the application guidelines). 
 
 
Notes  
• English proficiency certificates issued independently by universities or other educational 
institutions (e.g., CEFR B2 certification letters) will not be accepted. 
• Please note that this requirement differs from the English proficiency requirements for 
the SDW Program. 
• Applicants whose native language is English or who are enrolled in a degree program taught 
entirely in English must submit:  
Letter issued by their home institution confirming this status 
This requirement applies regardless of whether the applicant falls under Category A or 
Category B.

Important Changes and Notes Regarding the SDW : Sandwich 
Program (Coursework-Based Exchange) 
     NEW / Important Changes 
1. Graduate-Level Course Enrollment Restriction (Effective Spring 2027)   
 From Spring Semester 2027, undergraduate students participating in the SDW Program will 
no longer be allowed to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Students should consider this change when preparing study plans and discussing credit 
transfer arrangements with their home institution.  
 Until the Spring 2027 course list is published, students should refer to the current 
timetable for reference. 
 
2026 Grade 1 Exchange Program Exchange Program Student (Undergraduate) | Shibaura 
Institute of Technology Timetable Search 
 
 
2. Special Provision for Students from Five-Year Integrated Degree Programs 
 Students enrolled in integrated five-year degree programs may be considered academically 
equivalent to master's students during their senior years.  
 Eligible students may continue to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Partner institutions must explain which year(s) of their program are considered master's-
level equivalent.  
 Supporting documentation must be submitted through the TAO application system by the 
nominator. 
 
3. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
 Due to stricter immigration screening procedures, all student visa applicants must provide 
proof of financial capability.  
 Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be provided in 
the application system.  
 Supporting documents must be uploaded through the TAO application system.

original_evidence.text:
4. Research Activities for SDW Participants 
Eligibility 
 Only students enrolled in the SDW Program for two semesters (one academic year) are 
eligible. 
 
Requirements 
Students wishing to conduct research activities must: 
 Apply during the same application period as the REP (Research Exchange Program). 
 Obtain prior approval from the prospective academic supervisor (laboratory faculty 
member). 
 Submit the same application documents required for the REP Program, including:  
o Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
o Research Proposal 
o Any other required supporting documents 
 Pay the facility usage fee specified in the REP Program application guidelines. 
 
Important Notes 
 Research activities will only be permitted after all required application procedures have 
been completed and approved. 
 Final approval is subject to review by both the University and the prospective academic 
supervisor. 
 
 
5. No Extension of the SDW Program During Enrollment  
 
 Effective from Fall 2026, students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to extend 
their participation in the Sandwich Program during their period of enrollment. Applicants 
must carefully decide at the time of application whether to register for one semester or 
two semesters. 
 Please note that students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to switch from the 
Sandwich Program to the REP Program, as stated in Item 4 above.

original_evidence.text:
Important Changes and Notes Regarding the REP 
(Research Exchange Program) 
Please ensure that the following important information is communicated to students prior to 
nomination and application for the REP Program. 
 
     NEW / Important Changes 
 
1. Simultaneous Participation in the SDW Program (Coursework -Based Exchange Program) Is 
Not Permitted （NEW） 
 
Due to the increasing number of SDW participants, SIT expects that available course capacity 
will need to be prioritized for students officially enrolled in the SDW Program. As a result, it has 
become difficult to accommodate requests from REP students who wish to enroll in courses in 
addition to their research activities. Although REP students staying for one semester were 
previously allowed to take courses upon request, this arrangement will no longer be available. 
Accordingly: 
• Students participating in the REP (Research Exchange Program) are not eligible to 
participate in the SDW Program (coursework -based exchange program) at the same 
time. 
• Students admitted to the REP Program will engage exclusively in research activities . 
• Course enrollment will not be permitted  for REP students. 
 
 
2. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
Beginning in July 2026, the Immigration Services Agency of Japan will implement stricter 
screening procedures for student visa applications. As a result, all students applying for a 
student visa will be required to provide documentation demonstrating sufficient financial 
resources to support themselves during their stay in Japan. 
Accordingly: 
• All student visa applicants must submit financial support documentation. 
• Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be 
provided in the application system. 
• Detailed instructions regarding the required documents will be provided through the TAO 
Online Application System. Applicants will be required to upload the designated 
supporting documents through TAO.

original_evidence.text:
5. English Language Proficiency Requirement 
The required English proficiency documentation differs depending on whether the applicant has 
already obtained preliminary acceptance from a prospective academic supervisor. 
 
■ A: Applicants Who Have Obtained Preliminary Acceptance from a Prospective Academic 
Supervisor 
 
The applicant must submit either one of the following: 
• An official English-language proficiency test score listed in the application guidelines; or 
• An email from the prospective academic supervisor confirming:  
o their preliminary acceptance of the applicant; and 
o that the applicant possesses sufficient English proficiency to conduct research 
activities. 
 
 
■ B: Applicants Without a Designated Prospective Academic Supervisor  
The applicant must submit: 
• An official English proficiency test score demonstrating CEFR B2 level or above (e.g., 
TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, or another test specified in the application guidelines). 
 
 
Notes  
• English proficiency certificates issued independently by universities or other educational 
institutions (e.g., CEFR B2 certification letters) will not be accepted. 
• Please note that this requirement differs from the English proficiency requirements for 
the SDW Program. 
• Applicants whose native language is English or who are enrolled in a degree program taught 
entirely in English must submit:  
Letter issued by their home institution confirming this status 
This requirement applies regardless of whether the applicant falls under Category A or 
Category B.

！Important Information 
6. Course Load Requirement for Student Visa Eligibility  
To satisfy the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a student visa, students must attend 
classes totaling at least 600 minutes per week throughout the semester . 
 
 
7. Course Availability and Enrollment 
 Course offerings and enrollment capacities vary from year to year.  
 Enrollment in specific courses, including graduate -level courses, cannot be guaranteed.  
 Students should carefully consult with their home institution when planning their study 
abroad program.  
 This is particularly important for students who have:  
• specific degree requirements, 
• credit transfer objectives, or 
• graduation timelines that depend on particular courses.  
 
Course Timetables 
 Currently available timetables:  
• Spring Semester 2026 
• Fall Semester 2026 
 The Spring Semester 2027 timetable is scheduled to be released in March 2027.  
 Until then, students should use the 2026 timetables as a reference when preparing 
preliminary study plans. 
 
Courses with Enrollment Caps 
 Some courses have limited enrollment capacity.  
 Even if a course is open to exchange students, enrollment is not guaranteed.  
 Students are strongly encouraged to complete degree-critical courses at their home 
institution whenever possible. 
 
Architecture-Related Courses 
 Architecture-related courses are particularly competitive.  
 Enrollment capacity is often very limited.  
 Students may not be able to enroll in their preferred architecture courses even if those 
courses are listed as available.

original_evidence.text:
3. Extension of the Study Period 
Students Entering Japan with a Short-Term Visa 
 Students who participate in the program under a short-term visa are not eligible to extend 
their study period under any circumstances.  
 Students should carefully determine their intended period of study before submitting their 
application. 
 
Students Holding a Student Visa 
 Students who wish to extend their study period while holding a student visa must notify the 
International Office at least two months prior to their scheduled completion date.  
 Applicants seeking an extension are required to submit the prescribed application documents.  
 If the extension results in a total study period of 182 days or longer, an additional facility 
usage fee of JPY 47,000 will be charged.  
 Approval of an extension is subject to the University's review and procedures. 
 
 
！Important Information 
4. Selection of a Prospective Academic Supervisor  
SIT does not publish a directory of faculty contact information. In addition, the application 
process differs depending on the applicant's circumstances. Applicants should apply according 
to one of the following categories. 
■ Case 1: Applicants Who Have Obtained Prior Consent from a Faculty Member  
• This category applies to students who already have an academic connection with an SIT 
faculty member and have discussed the possibility of supervision in advance. 
• Applicants may designate that faculty member as their Prospective Academic Supervisor 
in their application. 
■ Case 2: Applicants Without a Prospective Academic Supervisor  
• This category applies to students who do not have an existing connection with an SIT 
faculty member. 
• Applicants may refer to the faculty list for applicants without a designated supervisor, 
which is available on the SIT website. 
• Applicants may indicate up to three preferred faculty members in order of preference in 
their application. 
• Based on the applicant's preferences and academic background, SIT will conduct the 
supervisor matching process.

範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，

資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

original_evidence.text:
JLPT-N3 is suggested 
Chuo does not request an official language proficiency score, but 
students must be able to take courses taught in either English or 
Japanese. 
* Students who wish to enroll in the Faculty of Science and 
Engineering are highly recommended to have a JLPT N3 certificate. 
* Some faculties such as the Faculty of Commerce and the Faculty of 
Science and Engineering do not offer courses in English. 
*Applicants for Graduate schools (except Science & Engineering) are 
required to prove Japanese language proficiency to take causes taught 
in Japanese.

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

original_evidence.text:
Exchange students at Kansai University follow the “KUGF (Kansai University Global 
Frontier) Curriculum”. Students whose Japanese language proficiency is sufficiently 
high can also take undergraduate courses offered by each faculty. 
The purposes of the KUGF curriculum are to improve language proficiency and 
communication skills, develop a high level of cross-cultural understanding, and foster 
global leadership skills. The curriculum can be categorized into 2 courses. 
Please refer to “KUGF Course Guide“ for contents of the courses and language 
requirements. 
依姐妹校不同 Module 之要求，詳細如下方 LINK 說明

National Central University

學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

⚫ 托福 TOEFL iBT/ITP

其他能力證明或個人作品(選繳)

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

簽名日期:_____________________

地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，

績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。

內容。

National Central University

學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。

E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。

內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

original_evidence.text:
Pukyong National University
Fact Sheet for Exchange Programs
 EXCHANGE PROGRAM INFORMATION
Courses Most of courses are taught in Korean, but a variety of courses 
are offered in English. The list of courses taught in English will 
be available one or two months prior to each semester. The list 
will be sent to all accepted exchange students by Email with 
instructions on course registration. Exchange students can take 
up to 18 academic credits per semester. If students would like 
to learn Korean Language, they could participate in the Korean 
Language Program during the semester with 30% discounted 
price.
All courses at PKNU are credit-bearing and are recognized by 
most universities and institutions.
Credit Transfer
Grading Scale
     Housing
However, it is better that students consult academic officials 
at their home universities about credit transfer prior to the 
program begins. It is students’ responsibility to consult 
properly, and it is their home university’s authority to decide 
on the credit transfer.
*3 Credit Hours: 45 contact hours
*2 Credit Hours: 30 contact hours

All exchange students are automatically assigned to a room 
(shared) at on-campus dormitories. The dormitory fee for one 
semester is around KRW 2,000,000 which includes three meals 
per day at the cafeteria. Students can find an accommodation 
outside the campus if they want.
National Health Insurance              All exchange students are required to enroll Korean National
Health Insurance. They will be automatically enrolled on the 
same day of alien registration after they arrive in Korea. They 
have to pay about KRW 100,000 per month. More detailed 
information will be provided to the accepted exchange 
students. Students staying in Korea for less than six months are 
not covered by Korean National Health Insurance. Therefore, 
they must obtain either international student or traveler 
insurance before departing for Korea to cover their entire stay. 
The university will not be responsible for any issues arising 
from insurance claims if students fail to secure proper 
coverage.
PKNU Student Buddy Program  PKNU student buddy will help exchange students adjust to a
new life at PKNU. The Buddy program application will be 
accepted at an exchange student orientation a few days before 
the start of the semester, after the students arrive in Korea.

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

簽名日期:_____________________

地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，

original_evidence.text:
Pre-Arrival Information
Course Registration
Once you are admitted to the University of Seoul as an exchange student, the coordinators of the OIA office will contact you directly and assist you with your course registration. You may register a course or drop a course online during the course change period, the first week of each semester. Normally, course registration and changes are done through the website at
http://wise.uos.ac.kr.
Unfortunately, since all the instructions are in Korean, you are advised to ask for your UOS Buddy’s help.
Notice
You must print out your confirmed course registration results shown on the computer screen of the online registration and submit it to your coordinator after the course change period ends.
Please check if your name is on the final class rosters.
If you do not follow the academic regulations and fail to confirm your online registration during this period, you will be responsible for any failure in taking a course and acquiring credits or dropping a course.
Courses Only for Exchange Students Offered by OIA office
All of the exchange students are strongly recommended to take Korean language courses and at least one course in Asian studies. You will be arranged to the Korean language courses on the basis of your Korean language proficiency. Asian Studies courses will be taught in English. Korean Language Courses cannot be registered by students online. OIA office will register your Korean Language courses collectively within the online course change period.
Notice
Please make sure that other courses registered do not coincide with Korean Language courses when you make any changes. In case you took Korean language level test, your schedule could be changed according to the result of the test.
Graduates students are not able to do the online course registration with these courses offered by OIA office. Please let your coordinator know if you take these courses.
Regular Courses Offered in English and in Korean
Some of the regular courses are offered in English, but many of them are in Korean. Some classes cannot be accessed because of academic regulations or class size. If this happens to you, you will need permission from the professor of the course. Please contact your coordinator at the OIA office for assistance concerning these matters. You can ask your UOS buddy where your classrooms are.
Transportation to UOS
1
Incheon International Airport
By Limousine Bus from Incheon International Airport
You are advised to find the bus stop "5B” at the exit of Incheon International Airport Terminal 1 and the bus stop “No.34” of Terminal 2.
The limousine, #6002, will take you to Cheongryangni, the bus's final destination. The fare of limousine is 17,000 KRW. You may
1) Get off at the Cheongryangni stop and take a taxi or take a bus to the University of Seoul, or 2) Wait a little while until the bus heads to the next stop and the next stop will be University of Seoul.
By Taxi/Call Van from Incheon International Airport
From the airport, it costs approximately 80,000 - 90,000 KRW by taxi up for 4 people to the University of Seoul. The fare of regular taxi starts from 4,800 KRW, while deluxe taxis start from 6,500 KRW.
By Subway from Incheon International Airport
You will have to make a transfer at Seoul station (line1).
Incheon International Airport Public Transportation Guide
2
Kimpo International Airport
By Subway from Kimpo International Airport
If your flight arrives at Kimpo International Airport you are advised to use subway (Line 5). Get off at Dapsimni station which is the closest station from University of Seoul and take a taxi to the University of Seoul at Exit 3 or 4. The taxi fare from Dapsimni station to the University of Seoul (pronounced 'Seoul Sirip Dae-hak-kyo', 서울시립대학교 in Korean) is around 7,000 KRW.
Gimpo International Airport Subway Usage Guide
By Taxi/Call Van from Kimpo International Airport시
From the airport, it costs approximately 40,000 - 50,000 KRW by taxi up for 4 people to the University of Seoul. The fare of regular taxi starts from 4,800 KRW, while deluxe taxis start from 6,500 KRW.

답변
For STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics), Architecture, Economics, and Design courses, enrollment is not guaranteed for exchange students whose majors are different.
Admission to these courses is reviewed case by case. Professors and academic staff will consider your major and academic record from your home university before approving enrollment.

- Electrical and Computer Engineering majors only
- Architecture majors only
- Materials Science and Engineering majors only
- Business majors only
During the course registration period, courses have a limited number of seats for exchange students. If a course is already full, you may only register if a seat becomes available during the first week of the semester.

Certificate of MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella)
To meet the requirements, your Certificate of MMR must include two clearly visible dates for your MMR vaccinations.
The certificate must be written in English, and your name, along with the two vaccination dates, should be clearly visible on a single page.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
If your local health department or hospital is unable to issue this certificate, you will need to consult with a doctor.
The doctor must provide a statement confirming that you have antibodies or clear indications of immunity from two MMR vaccinations.
If provided by a doctor, the medical certificate must include a statement confirming that you possess immunity antibodies from the second dose of the MMR vaccine.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Generally, as long as you have received two doses of the measles vaccination, it will be sufficient!
If you can provide your vaccination certificate, it will help expedite the verification process. (Highly recommended.)
Certificate of Health (Chest X-Ray Result or TB Test Result)
You will also need to provide a document from a hospital or clinic pertaining to a chest X-ray result or a TB (Tuberculosis) test result.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Please note that final approval is at the discretion of the dormitory team, so it is essential that all information, including the two vaccination dates, is clearly legible from their perspective.

National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) Enrollment and Important Information for International Students
1. Automatic Enrollment
Starting March 2021, all non-Korean international students, including exchange and visiting students, are mandatory and automatically enrolled in Korea’s National Health Insurance upon the date of alien registration.
2. Consequences of Non-Payment
Restrictions on Health Insurance Benefits
Health insurance benefits at medical institutions will be unavailable starting from the first day of the month following the payment deadline until the outstanding contributions are fully paid.
Restrictions on Visa Extension
Non-payment may result in the denial of visa extensions by the Korean Immigration Office.
Compulsory Collection
If the insurance contributions are not paid by the specified deadline, the NHIS may initiate compulsory collection procedures.
This may include seizing assets such as real estate, vehicles, bank deposits, etc.
3. Important Note
For all insurance-related inquiries, please contact the NHIS directly. Our office cannot assist with these matters.
NHIS Contact Information

.

Certificate of MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella)
To meet the requirements, your Certificate of MMR must include two clearly visible dates for your MMR vaccinations.
The certificate must be written in English, and your name, along with the two vaccination dates, should be clearly visible on a single page.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
If your local health department or hospital is unable to issue this certificate, you will need to consult with a doctor.
The doctor must provide a statement confirming that you have antibodies or clear indications of immunity from two MMR vaccinations.
If provided by a doctor, the medical certificate must include a statement confirming that you possess immunity antibodies from the second dose of the MMR vaccine.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Generally, as long as you have received two doses of the measles vaccination, it will be sufficient!
If you can provide your vaccination certificate, it will help expedite the verification process. (Highly recommended.)
Certificate of Health (Chest X-Ray Result or TB Test Result)
You will also need to provide a document from a hospital or clinic pertaining to a chest X-ray result or a TB (Tuberculosis) test result.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Please note that final approval is at the discretion of the dormitory team, so it is essential that all information, including the two vaccination dates, is clearly legible from their perspective.

courses.note: 一般學期最少6、最多20學分，15學分為建議；暑校最多8另屬短期，不套中央116一般學期。主要韩語授課，2026Fall英語課單只是參考，未取得2027課單、不保證開課或有座位。 Architecture／Design／Music專業課需事前核准；STEM／Economics等跨主修按背景與名額審查，部分課限原專業。Business優先本主修，Economics與Business不是同一學位；課滿不能保證例外加簽。 第一週加退選後須列印確認結果交coordinator及查final roster；韓語課由OIA依分級代註冊，研究生無法自行線上選OIA課時須告知coordinator。

original_evidence.text:
Courses offered in English
Exchange students can take up to 20 credits for a regular semester (spring or     fall) and up to 8credits for Seoul International Summer School. Most of the     courses offered during regular semesters are lectured in Korean, which can be     found at
UOS Website → Academics → Colleges → Courses
Courses List
List of Courses offered in English
→ Please click each course title and you can find its course description
→ The course list below is provided for reference only, and         the courses offered may vary each semester. Course availability depends on         individual course registration results, and enrollment is not guaranteed.         Therefore, we recommend that you keep flexibility in your academic planning.
→ Please note that major-specific courses offered by certain         departments—such as Architecture, Design, and Music—require prior         approval. If you wish to enroll in major courses from these departments, you         must confirm the availability after the course list is finalized each semester.

The Courses Lectured in English for Regular Semesters
Department
Course No
Course Title
Credit
Department of Sport Science
63011
Introduction to Adapted Physical Activity
This course is designed to provide an introduction to the field of adapted physical activity for exercise and sport science majors. The goal of this course is to gain a better understanding of various disability conditions and how physical activity can be accommodated to unique conditions of individuals with disabilities. This course covers legislation, etiology, principles and problems related to adapted physical activity programs, as well as sports for individuals with disabilities.
3
Department of Design
66350
Visual Communication DesignⅡ
This course is designed to develop well-organized visual abilities (especially 2D) and create a matured view of the production process of visual design to fit the concept.
3
School of Economics
28168
Economics of corporate finance
This course is for undergraduate students who have basic knowledge of economic concepts and methodologies, and covers the topics of capital structure and financial decision making under the valuation framework to provide understanding of corporate finance theory.
3
School of Economics
28015
Econometrics
Econometrics is a collection of research methods used to estimate and test economic relationships. The methods introduced in this course are also widely applied in business disciplines, including accounting, finance, marketing, and management, as well as in many areas of the social sciences.                               This course is designed to help bridge the gap between being “a student of economics” and becoming “a practicing economist.” Through this course, you will develop a broad understanding of the field and build intuition for how econometric methods work. The course will emphasize both a clear understanding of fundamental econometric tools and their practical application to real-world data and economic questions.                                                    By the end of this course, students should be comfortable with fundamental concepts in statistics and probability. They should be able to estimate and interpret linear regression models, critically evaluate regression results reported in applied academic research, and clearly explain empirical findings to audiences without formal training in economics.
3
School of Economics
28148
Asset pricing theory
The purpose of this course is to provide an opportunity to study the fundamental theory of pricing financial assets as an application of economic models and analytical frameworks.                               The use of AI is permitted in class, but its use in exam is strictly prohibited.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40138
Electrical and Computer Engineering Capstone Design
The main objective is to learn design and implementation methods for software projects. The students will follow an object-oriented software design process. During the first half of a semester, each team of two students will work on a different project. During the second half, each team is assigned to a part of a large project. To emphasize cooperative design and communication skills, students are required to have regular project meetings, make presentations, and publish associated documents. The students should be familiar with object-oriented programming.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
30034
Introduction to Algorithm
This course introduces the design and analysis of basic computer algorithms. Students will understand worst-case running time for an algorithm and its associated data structure. Covered topics are: sorting, searching, dynamic programming and advanced data structure.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40063
Signals and Systems
The objective of this course is to introduce the analytical tools and techniques needed for the design and analysis of continuous-time linear systems. The primary topics are convolution, transforms and sampling theory. Specifically, this course covers topics associated with the continuous time systems; classification of signals and systems, convolution, differential equations, Fourier series, Fourier transform, bilateral Laplace transform, and design and analysis of continuous-time linear systems with linear circuit examples. We also will discuss the introductory topics related with the discrete-time systems; Nyquist sampling theory, discrete-time processing of the continuous-time signals.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40070
Digital Signal Processing
The objective of this course is to present the analytical tools needed for the design and analysis of discrete-time systems. We will cover classifications of discrete-time signals and systems, convolution, difference equations. Also, this course deals with several transforms including bilateral Z-transforms, discrete-time Fourier transform, Discrete Fourier transform. Several tools for analyzing discrete-time signals and systems will be introduced in this course so that students can acquire the ability of analyzing and designing discrete-time systems.  Several topics will be given as programming projects to provide the experiences on the practical system design.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40087
Artificial Intelligence
This course introduces artificial intelligence problems and techniques applicable to intelligent systems. Topics included are: intelligent agents, problem solving, knowledge and reasoning, planning, uncertain knowledge and reasoning, and learning.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40095
Solid-State Physical Electronics
The lecture will provide a valuable theoretical introduction and an overview of the fundamental physics of solids, in particular semiconductors. This course includes crystal properties, atoms and electrons, Energy bands of semiconductors, and p-n junction structures.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40106
Embedded Systems Applications Design
This class covers the co-design of hardware and software which is the essential technology for the design of embedded systems. The kernel design, the device driver design, the I/O system design, and the VHDL design are introduced in this class.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40127
Applied Microprocessor Lab
In this experimental lecture, the fundamental operation, designing the peripheral circuit, and programming of microprocessor will be covered. Students will practice designing microprocessor peripheral circuits with FPGA. For term-project they have to design, and make microprocessor system and install OS into the microprocessor circuit.
2
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40137
Fabrication of Integrated Circuit
Integrated Circuits have been extensively employed in a variety of wide applications such as memory, communications systems, medical devices, home and industrial appliances. Recent rapid growth in electronics fields shows that Integrated Circuits play a more and more important role in next-generation automobiles, sensors, merged memory logic, and non-memory system applications.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40140
Introduction to Power Electronics
Students will learn fundamentals of the power diodes and switches for power conversion at the beginning. The topics of this class extend to analysis and design methods of the DC to DC, AC to DC, and DC to AC power converters using the power diodes and switches.
3
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
40166
Artificial Intelligence for Cellular Communications
This class offers various topics including overview of cellular communications and wireless channel characteristics, and highlights network architectures and fundamental technologies for cellular communication systems. Especially, this class emphasizes artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and services for 6G cellular communication systems. In addition, this class includes the following topics for prediction and classification in cellular communication environments: linear regression model, linear classification model, neural networks, and so on.
3
Department of Materials Science and Engineering
39044
Thermodynamics of Materials
The 1st, 2nd, and 3rd laws of thermodynamics are introduced, and then the reaction equilibria between condensed phase and gas phase and theory of solutions are studied.
3
Department of Materials Science and Engineering
39115
Materials Capstone Design
This course provides training on critical thinking and engineering design. The students are challenged to innovate and improve materials used in any engineering systems, and are also encouraged to pursue interdisciplinary studies. The students’ designs are expected to be creative enough to be filed as an international patent application so that their intellectual properties can be protected. Also, selected designs will be competed at international expositions.
3
Department of Materials Science and Engineering
39140
Design of Experiments for Materials AI
This course integrates computer programming skills with statistical data analysis and experimental design, which are essential foundations for scientific research and decision making, to understand basics of artificial intelligence.  Students will apply these techniques to an engineering design project at the end of the semester.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51250
Concepts and Uses of English Grammar
This course aims to give students a good understanding of how grammar is conceptualized and used in authentic contexts. Students learn the grammar of spoken and written English, improving their knowledge of English grammar. There are 15 sections; each section covers one area of English grammar like tenses, modals, nouns, verbs, determiners, finite clauses, non-finite clauses, conditionals, reported speech, and the like. Each section focuses on its uses of a grammatical pattern, and practical exercises and also explores grammatical contrasts between apparent similar grammatical patterns.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51252
AI and Logic in English
This course aims to introduce the intersection of artificial intelligence, theoretical semantics, and natural language logic. Students will learn various topics, including fundamental concepts of semantics and logic, principles of natural language processing, word vectorization, context understanding, semantic analysis, and logical form.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51257
English and cultures of the world
This course aims to explore the interaction between English and English-speaking cultures around the world. Students will engage with authentic materials such as films, novels, newspapers, and broadcasts, covering not only well-known varieties of English such as American, British, and Australian English, but also English in lesser-known areas such as India, Singapore, European nations, etc. Through synchronic and diachronic analysis, the course examines how English has influenced different cultures and, in turn, how cultural, social, and historical contexts have shaped the use and development of English. By comparing diverse national cases, students will gain a critical understanding of the global status of English, its regional variations, and the significance of English in processes of globalization and in contemporary.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51068
English Phonetics
This course aims to provide students with a thorough grounding in general English phonetics and help them to develop a practical ability to use the knowledge. This course also supplements insight and understanding about the important principles of American English pronunciation, through which they will acquire a theoretical and substantial basis for how English sounds are produced and how they are related with prosody such as stress and intonation. Students will have an opportunity to correct their pronunciation and finally have it evaluated.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51086
British and American Drama
This course is a survey of 19th and 20th century plays written by British and American playwrights. Representative dramatists from each literary-historical period and a range of dramatic style will be covered with the emphasis on modern drama. Along with analysis of dramatic texts, some attention will be paid to the theatrical, cultural and historical contexts. Selections from filmed productions will be shown periodically. The course will help students critically approach the cultural factors of performance texts and provide chances to interpret/rewrite/perform the plays from their own perspectives.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51193
Understanding of English Education
The present course is for students who are interested in learning how to teach English as Second Language effectively. It covers the theory and practice of teaching listening, speaking, reading, writing, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, discourse and assessment.                               Based on the knowledge they have acquired, students will analyze the current English textbooks used in secondary schools in Korea. They will identify the problems in the textbooks and possibly come up with the solution and detailed suggestions.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51201
English Presentation and Discussion
The course aims to study and learn the skills necessary to make a clear, well-organized, and successful presentation and discussion by strengthening their oral and aural English skills. They gain experience and confidence in being an active discussion participant and leader as well as a strong presenter.
3
Department of English Language and Literature
51223
English Practice
The primary objective of this course is to help students develop their speaking abilities and communicative competence through use of the language. To meet this aim, ample opportunities to practice the language by speaking in class and interacting with others will be provided. Although the major skills we will focus on are discussion and presentation, competence in other types of communication such as debates and surveys are also a part of the curriculum. Although the course is open to students of any level, the course is quite demanding in terms of the work required. Only students are willing and eager to put in a lot of work to develop their skills are encouraged to enroll. NOTE: This course SHOULD NOT be taken along with "English Interview & Presentation" (영어면접과발표) during the same semester.
3
Department of Statistics
47771
Machine Learning and Lab
In this course, learning methods based on R or Python often adopted in various learning problems are introduced. The topics includes supervised learning methods such as decision trees and neural networks and unsupervised learning methods such as association rules, clustering, and dimension reduction methods.
3
Department of Physics
45040
Physics and Computer II
In this course students will learn scientific programming. Short lectures on C++ will be given. Students will learn various aspects of OO languages, such as class design, inheritance, templates, File I/O, and data modeling, Students must successfully finish the series class, Physics and Computer I, in order to follow this course correctly.
3
Department of Physics
45111
Solid State PhysicsⅡ
This course is designed to study advanced topic of solid state materials including superconducting devcice (SQUID), para- and ferroelectricity, ferro- and antiferromagnetism, magnetic resonance, non-crystalline solid and point defect physics, surface and interface physics , also basic aspects of nano-size materials.
3
Department of Physics
45153
Applied Physics Experiment
The development and applications of Galileo's telescope gave birth to the field of optics. These laser and optical technologies have been used as the most important tools in physics, making it possible to experimentally prove numerous scientific phenomena and applied in many engineering fields.
3
College of Business Administration
27002
Accounting Principles
The course covers the objectives, basic theories, principles, and methods of accounting.  Students will measure and report financial positions regarding income, costs, and revenue. The course includes the framework for decision-making, recording processes, and accounting cycles.
3
College of Business Administration
27102
Consumer Behavior
This course aims to explore the importance of consumer behavior analysis from various perspectives in consumer-centered modern marketing, introducing models of consumer behavior from a behavioral science standpoint and researching the application and evaluation of each model. To achieve this, students will acquire and understand the theories and analytical techniques related to social and psychological factors in consumer information evaluation and decision-making processes, and develop the ability to apply these to real-world decision-making situations faced by consumers.
3
College of Business Administration
27105
Marketing Management
This course takes an analytical approach to the study of marketing problems of business firms and other organizations. Focus is placed on the influence of the marketplace and the marketing environment on marketing decision making; the determination of an organization's products, prices, channels and communication strategies; and an organization's system for planning and controlling its marketing efforts.
3
College of Business Administration
27301
Financial Management
The major topics of this course are as follows: the decision of the size of capital required by the firm, the planning about the timing and method of borrowing such capital, the optimal operation and management of the capital, and the theories and practices about these topics.
3
College of Business Administration
27302
Investment Theory
In this class, you will understand why you should invest in stocks. As an overarching concept, we learn that there are two types of risk in financial markets: good risks with expected returns and bad risks without expected returns. Portfolio theory teaches that investors can eliminate bad risk through diversification. The Nobel Prize-winning CAPM theory shows the relationship between good risk and expected return. Finally, we understand that it is very difficult to predict the direction of future stock prices through the efficient market hypothesis, which states that stock prices fully and immediately reflect relevant information.
3
College of Business Administration
27407
Human Resource Management
In a knowledge-driven global economy, organizations and managers have increasingly recognized that a critical source of competitive advantage stems from having an effective human resource system for obtaining, mobilizing, and managing the organization’s human resources. It is imperative that organizations understand the key HRM functions and how these functions should be aligned in order to gain competitive advantage through their people. Human Resource Management issues begin to appear from the very moment you hire someone for the first time, or you are hired by someone forthe first time. You will likely spend a major part of your life working for organizations as an employee, or, perhaps, leading one you have started. Also, you could become an HR professional. In any case, however, your knowledge and understanding on human resource management will help you succeed in your career, as an employee, a top manager, a business owner, or an HR professional.
3
College of Business Administration
27503
Managerial Accounting
This course covers the preparation and analysis of cost concepts, theories, and the implementation and evaluation of an accounting system as a source of information for internal users.   This course also includes an overview of decision making, planning, controlling, and evaluation of an organization.
3
College of Business Administration
27701
Management Information Systems
You will be ready and able to understand key business models, concepts, frameworks, and issues concerning IS and their use in business. You will be able to assess the current uses and value of IS in an organization, identify where IS can provide strategic advantage, and identify where firms and markets are vulnerable to being disrupted or severely compromised. You will have an understanding of the role of data, information, and knowledge in supporting the decision-making activities of the organization. You will be able to demonstrate how Excel and Access can be used for modeling and solving business problems.
3
College of Business Administration
27940
Financial Markets
The purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of the modern theory of financial intermediation so that the students can have conceptual and practical knowledge and skills for analyzing financial institutions and markets. There are three basic concepts to learn in this course: 1) information asymmetry, 2) risk in financial intermediation and 3) management of financial risk and related regulation. A considerable time will be spent on combining theories of information asymmetry and financial intermediation and their practical applications.
3
College of Business Administration
27964
Corporate Finance
This course is designed to help you develop a deeper understanding of the issues and the basic tools needed for corporate finance managers. The issues addressed in this course include how corporations raise capital, capital structure decisions, corporate valuations, mergers and acquisitions, and corporate governance. It is designed for students who has taken financial management course. This course will cover many cases on the issues being covered in the class.
3
Department of Urban Administration
11130

28167
Welfare economics
This course provides a theoretical analysis of how outcomes of resource                                         allocation studied in microeconomics can be evaluated from a social perspective.                                         Societies consist of individuals with diverse preferences and initial                                         endowments, and social preferences are formed by appropriately aggregating these                                         heterogeneous characteristics in order to evaluate allocation outcomes. The                                         course examines axiomatic properties that must be considered in social choice                                         problems and analyzes methods for deriving social preferences that satisfy these                                         axioms. It then applies axiomatic approaches to various resource allocation and                                         matching models to study the existence of desirable mechanisms and how such                                         mechanisms operate. The course primarily adopts a microeconomic- theoretic                                         approach and focuses on mathematical proofs and analysis. Students are therefore                                         strongly encouraged to have sufficient preparation for this type of material.                                         The required prerequisite is Microeconomics. The course is also closely related                                         to Economic Mathematics, Strategy and Information, Public Finance, Mathematical                                         Economics, and Advanced Microeconomic Theory (Associated competency:                                         microeconomic reasoning and real-economy analysis).

Certificate of MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella)
To meet the requirements, your Certificate of MMR must include two clearly visible dates for your MMR vaccinations.
The certificate must be written in English, and your name, along with the two vaccination dates, should be clearly visible on a single page.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
If your local health department or hospital is unable to issue this certificate, you will need to consult with a doctor.
The doctor must provide a statement confirming that you have antibodies or clear indications of immunity from two MMR vaccinations.
If provided by a doctor, the medical certificate must include a statement confirming that you possess immunity antibodies from the second dose of the MMR vaccine.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Generally, as long as you have received two doses of the measles vaccination, it will be sufficient!
If you can provide your vaccination certificate, it will help expedite the verification process. (Highly recommended.)
Certificate of Health (Chest X-Ray Result or TB Test Result)
You will also need to provide a document from a hospital or clinic pertaining to a chest X-ray result or a TB (Tuberculosis) test result.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Please note that final approval is at the discretion of the dormitory team, so it is essential that all information, including the two vaccination dates, is clearly legible from their perspective.
